A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DivEye research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-K support comparison despite reformatting, relocation and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DivEye evaluations on MAGE, RAID and HC3, plus feature ablations, backbone comparisons and adversarial experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and reports additional results on non-native and legal writing, text length, nucleus sampling and post-training objectives.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same nine surprisal features, frozen language-model feature extraction, XGBoost classifier and optional combination with existing detector scores. Equation 6 and Algorithm 1 retain the procedure. The 17-feature experiment in v3 Appendix F.3 is an ablation, not an adopted replacement.

E1.justification: v3 adds COREFL English essays by native German and Spanish speakers across proficiency levels A1-C2, and LEDGAR legal provisions (Appendix D.9). It also evaluates OLMo-3 outputs across post-training stages (Appendix F.4). These substantially extend the represented human populations, domains and generated data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding MAGE, RAID, boosting and Longformer comparisons. The new COREFL and LEDGAR evaluations reuse Binoculars and FastDetectGPT; no new competing detection method is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds TPR@FPR=5% evaluation and RAID AUROCs, relabelling existing RAID percentage columns from AvgAcc to TPR@FPR=5% in Tables 2-3 without establishing reruns. New protocols include 75/25 splits, 10-256-token truncation and 100 generations per top-p threshold. The detailed RAID Table 13 instead says FPR@TPR=5%, leaving its metric inconsistent.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained temporal-feature, leave-one-out, temperature and adversarial analyses, v3 adds proficiency and domain-score analyses, text-length sensitivity, top-p sensitivity and post-training comparisons. Appendix F.3 explicitly evaluates expansion to 17 features, supplying concrete evidence for diminishing returns that v1 mentioned only as preliminary findings.

E5.justification: Both versions report medians of three runs and random_state 42 in Appendix I, and retain the same paired-bootstrap feature-ablation procedure and p-values in Appendix D.6.1. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Many retained scores are identical, but v3 adds RAID AUROCs of 0.984 overall and 0.951 under attacks for DivEye, Testbed 8 TPR results, and new results including 82.07% on COREFL and 99.49% on LEDGAR. Table 2 now orders methods by AUROC, led by e5-small-lora, rather than v1's AvgAcc ranking led by Desklib AI. These are revised reporting and added evaluations, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1-6 and reasoning in Remark 1 are retained. The appendix proof sketch moves into Section 3.1 without substantive mathematical revision. The new Uniform Information Density discussion provides conceptual motivation rather than a new theorem, derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same detection, interpretability, efficiency, generalization and boosting claims, including improvements of up to 33.2% and 18.7%. Additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds a Uniform Information Density and burstiness explanation, attributes proficiency effects to richer rhythmic signatures, and explains legal-text detectability through domain-specific information peaks. It also interprets sampling and alignment effects and recommends stronger observer models for production sensitivity. The short-text limitation and nine-feature restraint were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds project-website and HuggingFace-demo access information, plus sampling, splitting and feature-expansion details for the new experiments. The code-release information, core XGBoost settings, 20 entropy bins, 1024-token limit and A100 hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations connecting the motivation to information density, burstiness and neural text degeneration, alongside references for COREFL, LEDGAR and OLMo-3. Appendix A and the broader positioning relative to watermarking, statistical detectors and fine-tuned detectors remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 relocates Remark 1 and its essay validation into the method section, makes localized explanatory and cross-reference edits, organizes added appendix analyses into subsections, and abbreviates illustrative text excerpts.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document typography and layout, restructures RAID tables with additional metrics and ordering, and adds four tables and Figures 12-16. The surprisal histogram moves from appendix Figure 8 to main-text Figure 2, and the detector-probability plot receives revised legends and an axis label.

improvement.justification: The new population checks and sensitivity analyses address important gaps in v1's validation. However, v3 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Table 5's 99.6% TPR at 5% FPR would require AUROC of at least 0.946 for the same ROC, whereas Table 1 retains 0.87 for the corresponding unseen-domain/model setting. Table 13 also reverses the TPR/FPR notation used in Tables 2-3. These problems affect confidence in the expanded evaluation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
